steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Whisk eggs, milk, flour, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and salt together in a bowl; set aside.
Melt butter in a 9x11-inch baking dish in the preheated oven, making sure it doesn't burn, about 5 minutes.
Pour batter into the baking dish with melted butter.
Continue baking until pancake is puffed and no longer moist in the center, 20 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: German Puff Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: This German puff pancake seven-ingredient recipe yields a puffy, oven-baked buttery pancake and is accented with the flavors of vanilla and cinnamon.
raw_recipe.name: German Puff Pancakes

review.reviewBody: Even though I'm German, I don't recognize this recipe but I have to say it is simple, delicious and filling. I half the recipe and bake in a small cast iron skillet right in the oven. Delicious as is or served with a light drizzle of syrup. I have also made this, sans the vanilla and cinnamon, as a vegetable pancake with sautéed mushrooms and onions. This makes much more than one serving LOL!

Made as recommended with these exceptions: added 2 tbsp sugar to make it sweet and added some baking powder. I used my mixer to get the eggs fluffy (pinch of cream of tartar or lemon juice helps!) And then added the dry to the wet and mixed well. I preheated the oven with a 9 inch cast iron skillet to start and added the butter when it was hot. Then gently poured in the mixture. The butter will brown immediately so make sure you're ready to dump in your batter or it is burned. Make sure your oven is hot and your pan/butter is sizzling. I also made a sweet vanilla whipped cream that I purposely over whipped to get it extra thick. Sprinkled cinnamon sugar and had a dollop of cream. Such a great treat! You'll notice that it will sink as it cools. Still so good. The sides were probably 4 inches and the center 2. Then it sank by half. Could be my error but we loved it so no complaints.

I just made this today. I added 1 tsp of ground ginger and upped the cinnamon to 1 tsp also. I used Plain Soy milk also and whipped the whole thing using an electric beater. The flavor was excellent and I'll definitely make again! We used vanilla yogurt and sliced bananas on it (my twin 8 year old girls loved it). It's definitely a winner!!

I can't imagine anyone down-rating this recipe. It's fool-proof and the best thing is it has no sugar except what you put on top. I divide the default quantity between two 10-inch cast iron skillets, and it serves 4-6 people. Preheat the skillets with the butter in the oven while you mix the rest. Traditionally served with a sprinkling of lemon juice and powdered sugar, or you can make a fancy dessert by ladling on any kind of fresh fruit or fruit pie filling. It could be a dinner or brunch dish, too, if you serve it with veggies and mushrooms or creamed chicken or beef or even fish. You won't be sorry you tried this!

I make this recipe all the time but with some additions that my family LOVES!
1 - I increase the eggs to 8 just to make it stick to the ribs a little more.
2 - I line the bottom completely with thinly sliced apple (1/2cm at peel side) before pouring the batter over top. The apples then float to the top a little and even more while baking.
3 - We eat this with plain yogurt and real maple syrup which is such a nice contrast.
4 - As one of the other reviews mentioned, this takes my oven quite a bit more than 20-25 minutes to bake.

This is definitely not light and airy as a regular pancake. That said they are delicious and eggy. I used a bit more butter in the baking dish, added a teaspoon of sugar and a bit of nutmeg with the cinnamon, then after I poured the batter in the baking dish topped it with 2 teaspoons of sugar and slivered almonds. Be sure to cook it long enough - the edges should rise up and even curl, but the center needs to be fully cooked. Yummy!

Used this as a base recipe. I live alone so halved all the ingredients except the cinnamon, which I doubled(would have used 3 tsp with the full recipe) and 1/4 tsp nutmeg ( 1/2 tsp for full recipe) and topped with apple slices. When halved the baking time drops to about 15 minutes, so keep an eye on it.

Since I was eager to try the recipe, but didn't need to cook for 6, I decided to scale it down to the following: 2 eggs, 1/3 cup flour, pinch salt, sprinkle of cinnamon, 1/3 cup milk, 1 1/2 tsp Smart Balance (instead of butter) in a small cast iron skillet in my large toaster oven. I left out the vanilla. Results were great. I loved seeing the pancake puff up and toast. I ate it with a little sorghum syrup. Thanks for the recipe.

I was surprised in a very good way by these! I've neither made nor had baked pancakes before so I didn't know what to expect, and these definitely have me impressed. I halved the recipe for my boyfriend and I and made it in a smaller pan, so they may have been thicker than usual, but I liked them that way. Reminded me of French toast, but chewier. We both decided that these would taste great done in little yorkie pans (or muffin pans) to make them individual and then stuff them with bacon or sausage. As it was this morning, we topped ours with honey, peanut butter, and bananas (not all at once though). I also sprinkled cinnamon sugar on the whole thing as soon as it came out of the oven, and that turned out to be a great addition. Looking forward to experimenting with this recipe!

I made this recipe for my family for dinner and it was a hit! I doubled the recipe and cooked half in muffin tins and half in a 9x13 pan. I used gluten free flour and it came out perfectly! It was very filling, delicious and we had many different toppings like strawberries, powdered sugar, whipped cream and syrup. Can wait to make again with apples or other variations

you can also get some fresh apples, peel, core and slice and cook them in butter till tender. Then place the apples first then batter on top in a cast iron skillet and bake. Very good. Thank you for sharing recipe.
I have made this recipe dozens of times. I use a glass 9x13” dish. Top with fruit, yogurt or just jam. Great as leftovers too. Quicker & easier than your usual pancakes and more protein.
Delicious! I served it with blueberry sauce. A big hit with my family.
Best with just syrup. Nutella/strawberries okay, too. 1/2 is square pan.
These are always a hit and are very quick and easy.
It's like if a pancake and french toast had a baby!

My mom has a recipe for german pancakes, and hers is very similar in that it has the same measurements of egg, flour and milk. Her recipe has a lot more butter and no vanilla or cinnamon. This recipe tasted very good. However, it didn't have any more "puff" than my mothers recipe. We like to put jelly and powdered sugar on my mothers german pancakes, but this recipe tastes fine with just sugar on top.

I have been making this for years. It’s my grandmothers recipe. Huge tip leave cinnamon out and whisk all ingredients ingredients the entire time butter is Browning open oven pull out rack the dishes on pour in your batter push rack back in gently turn the oven light on and stay out of the kitchen to prevent it from flopping. ONLY USE whole milk

I've made this many times, as written, and it's always a favorite. 5 stars, as is.

Today, I had already cracked the eggs and mixed the wet ingredients when I discovered I was out of flour. I substituted 1c old fashioned oats. Try it, it's just as delicious, the kids were still happy, and it's probably more filling.
Baked as written. Excellent! I doubled the recipe and fed three kids under 10, two teenagers, and two adults with some leftover. Very cheap and filling!
